_meta.spec: OVCA_Decision_Engine_Spec_v0.1 §3, with the tier scheme amended in SPEC.md 'Decisions taken'
_meta.scope: HGSC only. Every efficacy number here is copied from data/trials.json (vault note OVCA_HGSC_Algorithm_v1.2, full-text checked 2026-09-14); every toxicity number from data/tox.json; every label rule from data/labels.json. Nothing is written from memory.

tiers.1: OS benefit, replicated (≥2 randomised trials or a class effect confirmed by non-inferiority)
tiers.2: OS benefit, single phase 3 (CI excludes 1 as printed)
tiers.3: OS benefit only in a prespecified subgroup, or confounded by crossover / borderline
tiers.4: PFS/RFS benefit only; no OS benefit shown
tiers.5: No efficacy difference vs the standard (non-inferior / NS): chosen on toxicity, schedule or route
tiers.7: Do not use: OS worse, or PFS significantly worse than control

risk_flags.ild_or_pneumonitis: history of ILD/pneumonitis or current pulmonary compromise
risk_flags.ocular_disease: active ocular condition / chronic corneal disorder
risk_flags.gi_fistula_or_obstruction_risk: bowel involvement on imaging, prior perforation/fistula, subocclusion
risk_flags.uncontrolled_htn_or_proteinuria: BP not controlled on medical management, or proteinuria ≥2 g/24 h
risk_flags.cytopenia_baseline: not recovered to ≤G1 from prior chemotherapy (ANC <1500 or platelets <100k)
risk_flags.surgery_within_28d: major surgery within 28 days or unhealed wound

rule_effects.exclude: label contraindication, or the trial excluded this patient and the label mandates permanent discontinuation at any grade
rule_effects.caution: label hold/reduce threshold is close to the patient's baseline, or trial excluded this patient without a label rule

regimens.name: Carboplatin + paclitaxel × 6 cycles

tox_ref.note: G3/4 neurotoxicity 11% (6 cycles) vs 2% (3 cycles)

qualifiers: ACTION: benefit confined to non-optimally staged patients; none after optimal staging
Six cycles over three rests on an exploratory GOG-157 serous subset (recurrence HR 0.33, interaction p=0.04)

risk_rules.reason: Label: severe neuropathy → 20% dose reduction; no graded ladder
Label: do not treat solid tumours with baseline neutrophils <1,500/mm³
Label Table 17: transaminases ≥10×ULN or bilirubin >5×ULN → not recommended

regimens.name: Carboplatin + paclitaxel × 3 cycles

tox_ref.note: G3/4 neurotoxicity 2% vs 11% with 6 cycles

pfs.text: Recurrence HR 0.761 (0.51–1.13) for 6 vs 3, NS overall; serous subset favours 6

qualifiers: Non-serous histotypes gained nothing from 6 cycles (HR 0.94); in serous the exploratory subset favoured 6

tox_ref.note: Grade ≥2 neuropathy 15.5% vs 6%

exclude_default.reason: No recurrence or survival benefit (GOG-175); adds neuropathy

regimens.name: Carboplatin AUC 5–6 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m² q3w × 6

tox_ref.note: ICON8 arm 1: 42% any G≥3 (vs 62% / 53% weekly arms)

os.median: GOG-158 carbo/pac vs cis/pac: 57.4 vs 48.7 mo, non-inferior; platinum–taxane itself: GOG-111 38 vs 24 mo, RR 0.6 (0.5–0.8)

qualifiers: OS evidence is class-level: platinum–taxane beat platinum–cyclophosphamide (GOG-111), and carboplatin was non-inferior to cisplatin with less GI/renal toxicity (GOG-158)

risk_rules.reason: Label: severe neuropathy → 20% dose reduction; SCOTROC-1 docetaxel arm had less neuropathy (11% vs 30% ≥G2)
Label: CrCl <15 mL/min, data too limited for a recommendation

regimens.name: IV paclitaxel + IP cisplatin 100 + IP paclitaxel D8 (optimally debulked stage III)

tox_ref.note: Leukopenia G3/4 76% vs 64%; only 42% completed 6 IP cycles; catheter complications main reason for stopping

qualifiers: Not reproduced in the bevacizumab era: GOG-252 found no PFS or OS difference for IP carboplatin or IP cisplatin
Only 42% completed 6 IP cycles

Label §2.5: consider permanent discontinuation for grade 3–4 neuropathy; baseline G2 leaves no margin

tox_ref.note: ICON8 arm 2: 62%; JGOG-3016 G3/4 anaemia 69% vs 44%; JGOG discontinuation for toxicity 36% vs 22%

qualifiers: Did not travel: MITO-7, ICON8 (69% HGSC) and GOG-262 were all negative. The one concordant signal is GOG-262 without bevacizumab (PFS HR 0.62, stratified subgroup)
Japanese population (55% serous) and the bevacizumab interaction are the leading explanations; neither is proven

risk_rules.reason: Label: severe neuropathy → 20% reduction; weekly schedule adds cumulative exposure
Label: baseline neutrophils <1,500/mm³; JGOG anaemia G3/4 69%

regimens.name: Weekly carboplatin AUC 2 + paclitaxel 60 mg/m² × 18

tox_ref.note: G3–4 neutropenia 42% vs 50%; ≥G2 neuropathy 6% vs 17%; ≥1 dose reduction 19% vs 36%; QoL better; discontinuation 8% vs 4%; ICON8 weekly-both arm 53% any G≥3

risk_rules.reason: Label §2.9: discontinue for GI perforation, fistula; trials excluded bowel involvement
Label §2.9: withhold for severe hypertension not controlled medically / proteinuria ≥2 g/24 h
Label §2.9: discontinue for congestive heart failure
Label §2.1: do not administer until ≥28 days after major surgery and adequate wound healing

tox_ref.note: 57% vs 51% (both arms on bev); olaparib discontinuation 20%; dose reduction 41%

regimens.name: Bevacizumab maintenance alone (continued from chemotherapy)

tox_ref.note: ICON7 65% vs 54% (whole regimen); hypertension, proteinuria, GI perforation

pfs.text: GOG-0218 HR 0.717; ICON7 HR 0.81; effect HRD-independent

regimens.name: Durvalumab + olaparib + bevacizumab (non-tBRCAm)

tox_ref.note: 72.0% vs 62.0% control; immune-mediated AE 31.0% vs 10.6%; olaparib discontinuation 16.7%

os.median: Interim ITT 48.5 vs 48.0 mo, NS; HRD+ 0.84 (21% maturity)

qualifiers: Durvalumab alone adds nothing (HR 0.87, NS); durvalumab label not extracted in labels.json

tox_ref.note: TRAE G≥3 66% vs 51%; discontinuation 31%; 4 treatment-related deaths with pembro + olaparib

Trial exclusion; label has no contraindication

tox_ref.note: GOG-0213 chemo arm 75%; ICON4 G2–4 neuropathy 20% vs 1%, alopecia 86%

qualifiers: Only recurrence chemotherapy trial with an OS gain; benefit consistent in the ~34% with prior paclitaxel (no interaction)

regimens.name: Carboplatin + PLD 30 mg/m² q4w

regimens.name: Add bevacizumab to the platinum doublet, then maintenance to progression

tox_ref.note: GOG-0213 96% vs 75%; OCEANS 89.5% vs 82.4%; MITO-16B 79% vs 69%; bev discontinuation 20–25%

os.median: GOG-0213 42.2 vs 37.3 mo, P=0.056 (post hoc corrected-PFI HR 0.823, 0.680–0.996); OCEANS HR 0.95; MITO-16B 0.99

pfs.text: OCEANS HR 0.484; GOG-0213 0.628; MITO-16B 0.51 (after prior bev)

regimens.name: Olaparib maintenance after response to platinum

tox_ref.note: SOLO2 G3 32% + G4 4% (worst grade per patient, summed); Study 19 capsules 35.3%; SOLO2 discontinuation 11% → 17% final; fatal MDS 3 + AML 3

pfs.text: SOLO2 (gBRCAm) 19.1 vs 5.5 mo, HR 0.30; Study 19 (any BRCA) 8.4 vs 4.8, HR 0.35

regimens.name: Niraparib maintenance after response to platinum

tox_ref.note: NORA (ISD 200 mg) 50.8%, dose reduction 59.9%, discontinuation 4.0%; NOVA (300 mg fixed) 74.1%, G3–4 thrombocytopenia 33.8%

regimens.name: Rucaparib maintenance after response to platinum

tox_ref.note: 56% (63% final) vs 15%; dose reduction 55%; discontinuation 13%; MDS/AML 4% vs 3% final

os.median: BRCAm 45.9 vs 47.8 mo; HRD and ITT HR 1.0; 41% placebo later PARPi

pfs.text: BRCAm 16.6 vs 5.4 mo, HR 0.23; HRD 0.32; LOH-high 0.44; LOH-low 0.58; ITT 0.36

regimens.name: PARP inhibitor as treatment instead of chemotherapy

tox_ref.note: ARIEL4 59% vs 38%; SOLO3 50% vs 47%; MDS/AML 2–3%
